title: Peek-prefetch proxy experiments
content:
Purpose
This is a lightweight PRD-style experiment notebook proposing a "peek+prefetch" proxy concept for the Hosted API. The goal is to reduce perceived latency for tool-heavy streaming calls (tool calls, function hooks, structured extraction) without sacrificing correctness or SDK ergonomics. This doc captures UX ideas, API sketches, telemetry needs, rollout guardrails, and open questions for a small lab prototype.

Context / problem
- Customers build streaming calls that often need subsequent tool invocations (search, DB, external APIs) based on partial generation. In many cases we observe a common pattern: the model signals a next tool call early (intents, entities) but due to network roundtrips we only start the tool after full output chunking, increasing tail latency.
- Existing solutions: speculative local tool emulators, client-side prefetch, or blind microbatches. Each has tradeoffs: emulator drift, duplicate work, and SDK complexity.

Key idea: "peek+prefetch" proxy
- Client SDK exposes a lightweight peek() hint channel alongside streaming tokens. The server runtime and a proxy layer use short-lived intent hypotheses (peek frames) to prefetch tool inputs or warm dedicated tool connections in a speculative microbatch.
- Prefetch actions are non-destructive and idempotent: they fetch/prepare (cache keys, KV results, DB rows, embeddings) but do not mutate authoritative systems until a committed tool call arrives.
- When the model emits an actual tool call frame, the runtime validates hypotheses, promotes prefetched artifacts to the call, and proceeds with the normal tool invocation. If hypotheses are wrong, the proxy cancels or discards prefetched state.

User-facing SDK ergonomics (sketch)
- Streaming call pattern (pseudo-API):
  - client.streamPredict({prompt}) returns a StreamHandle
  - StreamHandle.on("peek", (hint) => { /* observed peek frames with confidence */ })
  - StreamHandle.on("partial", (tokens) => {})
  - StreamHandle.confirmToolCall(toolDescriptor, args)  // called by runtime when final structured call arrives

- peek() semantics:
  - lightweight JSON hint: {type: "search_hint", query: "invoice 123", confidence: 0.72, keys: ["invoice:123"]}
  - SDK default: do nothing unless the developer opts-in to prefetch via a single flag per stream or global client config (opt-in reduces unexpected costs).
  - Opt-in levels: none | warm-connections | fetch-only | fetch-and-cache-local (for embedded devices).

Proxy/runtime responsibilities
- Maintain a bounded speculative queue per stream. Each peek item has TTL and confidence threshold.
- Coordinate with tool adapters: prefetch should use read-only, non-mutating endpoints. Tool adapters expose a prefetch API surface (prepare(), cancel(), promote()).
- Track billing attribution separately for speculative work vs committed calls to avoid customer confusion and to enable safe quotas.

Structured output and correctness model
- Structured tool call frames (canonical JSON) remain the source of truth. Peek frames are hints only and must never be treated as authoritative.
- On promote: runtime computes checksum of prefetched payload vs actual args to ensure compatibility. If mismatch, runtime either re-fetches synchronously or falls back to non-prefetched path.
- In streaming scenarios where partial output is used for client UI, SDKs should expose whether content used prefetched artifacts to allow developers to indicate provisional versus final results.

Performance model and telemetry
- Key metrics to measure in experiments:
  - median and p95 tool-call latency (committed) with and without peek prefetch
  - wasted speculative effort ratio: speculative time/token-cost that is never promoted
  - promotion hit rate: fraction of prefetched artifacts reused
  - user-visible quality regressions (wrong data used) and number of rollbacks
  - SDK surface ergonomics: developer adoption and error rates in labs
- Instrumentation: fine-grained logs with stream id, peek id, confidence, prefetch start/end, promote, cancel. Tag events with customer id and model version for A/B analysis.

Safety, cost, and guardrails
- Default opt-in=false. Customers must enable peek-prefetch per-client or per-route.
- Hard caps per-account: speculative CPU/IO budget per minute; automatic throttling when budget exceeded.
- Prefetchable tool adapter whitelist: only read-only adapters allowed initially (search, embeddings lookup, cache fetch, DB read). No writes, no billing-sensitive endpoints.
- Billing: separated line items; speculative work billed at reduced rate or free up to a quota during beta. Clear console telemetry for speculative vs final cost.

Rollout plan (phases)
- Phase 0: lab prototype inside hosted-api sandbox. Implement minimal peek relay, single adapter for embeddings prefetch. Run tests against synthetic workloads.
- Phase 1: internal dogfood with a small set of product teams (console autosuggest, developer-playground). Monitor promotion hit rate and regressions.
- Phase 2: limited customer beta with opt-in routes and whitelist of adapters. Billing visibility active.
- Phase 3: general availability with expanded adapters and guardrail tuning.

Developer experience and docs
- Example guides: enabling peek-prefetch in Node, handling provisional UI states, testing for mismatches.
- SDK ergonomics: ensure peek event handlers are lightweight and non-blocking. Provide server-side fallback flags to disable prefetch when promotion rate falls below threshold.

Open questions / risks
- When model emits multiple competing hints, how to prioritize prefetch budget? Heuristic options: highest confidence, earliest timestamp, highest estimated cost-to-latency (i.e., prefetch expensive ops first).
- How to prevent data freshness mismatch (prefetched DB row might be stale by promote)? Consider short TTL and checksum verification on promote.
- UX complexity: exposing provisional vs final signals increases surface area for developers; how to present defaults that are easy to use?
- Billing pushback: customers may be surprised by speculative costs even if billed at lower rate. We need clear console messaging and default free quota.

Experiment checklist (short)
- [ ] Build peek frame proto and adapter prefetch interface (prepare/cancel/promote)
- [ ] Add instrumentation events and dashboard prototype
- [ ] Implement Node and Python SDK hooks for peek events and opt-in config
- [ ] Run microbenchmarks (embeddings prefetch, DB read patterns)
- [ ] Dogfood internally and collect promotion hit/miss metrics

Notes to reviewers
- This doc is intentionally exploratory. Focus on whether API primitives are low-friction for SDK users and whether the runtime-level promote/cancel model feels implementable for tool adapters.
- Related tickets: JIRA-API-3472 (prefetch plumbing), CONFLUENCE-9123 (adapter prefetch patterns).

TODOs
- Add sequence diagrams for stream <-> proxy <-> adapter flows (Jordan)
- Prototype a cancelation backchannel for long-running prefetches (Elliot)
- Pricing recommendation draft for beta (Priya)

End of note.
